mcqs.q: Oral diagnosis is best defined as the:
opts: Art and science of identifying an oral disease from its symptoms and signs
Surgical removal of an oral disease
mcqs.explain: Oral diagnosis is the art and science of identifying an oral disease from its symptoms and signs.

mcqs.q: The word 'diagnosis' comes from Greek meaning:
mcqs.explain: Diagnosis is Greek: dia = through, gnosis = knowledge.

mcqs.q: A 'symptom' differs from a 'sign' in that a symptom is:
opts: Subjective — felt and reported by the patient
A visible change noticed on examination
mcqs.explain: A symptom is subjective (reported by the patient); a sign is a visible change noticed during examination.

mcqs.q: The correct order of the diagnostic process is:
opts: History → examination → provisional diagnosis → investigations → final diagnosis
mcqs.explain: The diagnostic process: history → examination → provisional diagnosis → investigations → final diagnosis.

mcqs.q: In the diagnostic process, the diagnosis made BEFORE investigations is the:
mcqs.explain: A provisional diagnosis is made after examination and before investigations; the final diagnosis follows the investigations.

mcqs.q: A case history is best described as a:
opts: Planned professional conversation between patient and dentist
mcqs.explain: A case history is a planned professional conversation between patient and dentist — the foundation for diagnosis and a good relationship.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised METHOD of obtaining the patient's history?
opts: Interview, health questionnaire, or a combination
mcqs.explain: History is obtained by interview, a health questionnaire (a fixed set of health-related questions), or a combination of both.

mcqs.q: A 'health questionnaire' is:
opts: A fixed set of health-related questions
A free-form essay by the patient
mcqs.explain: A health questionnaire is a fixed set of health-related questions.

mcqs.q: Demographic data (registration number, name, etc.) primarily serve:
opts: Identification, record-keeping, legal documentation and billing
mcqs.explain: Demographic data are used for identification, record-keeping, legal documentation, progress tracking and billing/insurance.

mcqs.q: Addressing a patient by NAME is important mainly because it:
mcqs.explain: Using the patient's name provides personalized care — it builds trust and establishes good rapport.

mcqs.q: Knowing the patient's AGE helps with all of these EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: Age guides age-specific diagnosis/treatment, drug/anaesthesia dosage and consent (guardian for minors) — not the clinic's rent.

mcqs.q: For a minor, the patient's age is important because it determines:
mcqs.explain: Age affects legal/consent requirements — minors require guardian consent.

mcqs.q: Which conditions are particularly associated with FEMALE patients in the history?
opts: Pregnancy/pubertal gingivitis, lichen planus, autoimmune disorders
mcqs.explain: Females: pregnancy & pubertal gingivitis, lichen planus, autoimmune disorders, smaller body weight (lower dose), and drug caution in pregnancy/lactation.

mcqs.q: Which is more associated with MALE patients?
mcqs.explain: Males are noted for haemophilia and oral cancer.

mcqs.q: Recording the patient's ADDRESS is useful for epidemiology because it can reveal:
opts: Geographical prevalence such as endemic fluorosis
mcqs.explain: Address aids epidemiological studies of endemic/geographical diseases — e.g. fluorosis; caries is commoner in industrial areas, periodontal disease in rural areas.

mcqs.q: Gingival staining from lead or bismuth, or bruxism from a high-stress job, are gathered under which heading?
mcqs.explain: Occupation reveals occupational hazards — chemical/dust exposure, lead/bismuth gingival staining, stress-related bruxism/TMJ and habits.

mcqs.q: The 'chief complaint' is:
opts: The patient's primary concern for which they sought the dentist
mcqs.explain: The chief complaint reflects the primary concern/problem for which the patient approached the dentist.

mcqs.q: The chief complaint should be recorded:
opts: In the patient's own words and in chronological order
mcqs.explain: The chief complaint is recorded in the patient's own words, in chronological order.

mcqs.q: If a patient has MORE THAN ONE complaint, they should be recorded:
mcqs.explain: When there is more than one complaint, record them in the order of severity.

mcqs.q: The 'history of present illness' (HOPI) is:
opts: A chronological narrative of the problem from onset to the present
A list of all the patient's relatives
mcqs.explain: HOPI is a narrative account of the patient's problem from onset to present, listing symptoms, signs and treatment chronologically.

mcqs.q: The three common presentations analysed in the HOPI are:
mcqs.explain: HOPI commonly analyses pain, swelling and ulcer.

mcqs.q: When pain spreads from the tooth to the ear and temple, this property of pain is called:
mcqs.explain: Localization of pain may be localized, diffuse, referred or radiating; spread to the ear/temple is radiating/referred pain.

mcqs.q: Describing pain as 'burning, stabbing, shooting or sharp' records its:
mcqs.explain: The nature (character) of pain is recorded as burning, stabbing, shooting or sharp.

mcqs.q: Grading pain as 'mild, moderate or severe' records its:
mcqs.explain: Intensity of pain is graded mild, moderate or severe.

mcqs.q: Pain described as 'continuous or intermittent' refers to its:
mcqs.explain: Frequency of pain is continuous or intermittent.

mcqs.q: The PAST DENTAL HISTORY is taken mainly to:
opts: Evaluate current dental status and predict the patient's response to treatment
mcqs.explain: Past dental history evaluates the patient's current dental status and how they will respond to the proposed treatment.

mcqs.q: Which belongs in the PAST DENTAL HISTORY?
opts: Past experience with local anaesthesia and extractions
mcqs.explain: Past dental history includes visit frequency, past LA/extraction experience, periodontal/orthodontic therapy, RCT, appliances and surgery.

mcqs.q: The PAST MEDICAL HISTORY is important chiefly because:
opts: Many systemic diseases have oral manifestations and affect treatment
mcqs.explain: Many systemic problems have oral manifestations, so past medical history is essential for diagnosis and safe treatment.

mcqs.q: Reviewing 'cardiovascular, respiratory, CNS, GI, endocrine…' systems is part of the:
mcqs.explain: The past medical history reviews body systems — cardiovascular, respiratory, CNS, GI, genitourinary, musculoskeletal and endocrine.

mcqs.q: Hereditary diseases such as haemophilia, diabetes and hypertension are explored under:
mcqs.explain: Family history records inherited & familial diseases (e.g. haemophilia, diabetes mellitus, hypertension) plus marital/social status.

mcqs.q: Tooth-cleaning aids and technique (brush/finger, paste/powder, charcoal, salt) are recorded under:
mcqs.explain: Oral hygiene habits (cleaning aid and technique) are part of the personal history.

mcqs.q: Bruxism, tongue thrusting and mouth breathing are classified as:
mcqs.explain: Parafunctional habits — bruxism, tongue thrusting, mouth breathing, nail/cheek/lip biting — are recorded in the personal history.

mcqs.q: Smoking and chewing tobacco are recorded as:
mcqs.explain: Tissue-abuse habits — smoking and chewing tobacco (type/frequency/duration) — belong in the personal history.

mcqs.q: Which HOPI features are specifically analysed for an ULCER?
opts: Location, duration, onset, pain, discharge, whether recurrent
mcqs.explain: For an ulcer, the HOPI records location, duration, mode of onset, pain, discharge, whether it is recurrent, and any associated symptom.

mcqs.q: Overall, the case history is important because it:
opts: Forms the foundation for diagnosis and a successful patient–dentist relationship
mcqs.explain: The case history constitutes the foundation for an intelligent approach to diagnosis and establishes a successful patient–dentist relationship.

saqs.q: Define diagnosis, and differentiate a symptom from a sign.
saqs.a: Oral diagnosis = the art & science of identifying an oral disease from its symptoms and signs (Greek: dia = through, gnosis = knowledge). A symptom is subjective — felt/reported by the patient; a sign is an objective, visible change noticed during examination.

saqs.q: List the five steps of the diagnostic process in order.
Name the three methods of obtaining a patient's history.
saqs.a: Interview, health questionnaire (a fixed set of health-related questions), and the combined method.

saqs.q: Why is the patient's AGE important in the dental case history?
saqs.a: Age guides diagnosis & treatment planning (age-specific conditions), growth & development monitoring, safe medication/anaesthesia dosage, and consent requirements (guardian consent for minors).

saqs.q: How should the chief complaint be recorded?
saqs.a: In the patient's own words, in chronological order; if there is more than one complaint, in order of severity.

saqs.q: List the parameters used to analyse PAIN in the HOPI.
saqs.a: Location, onset (sudden/gradual), cause, duration, localization (localized/diffuse/referred/radiating), nature (burning/stabbing/sharp), intensity (mild/moderate/severe), frequency (continuous/intermittent), aggravating & relieving factors, and associated symptoms.

saqs.q: Why is the past medical history important, and which systems are reviewed?
saqs.a: Because many systemic diseases have oral manifestations and affect treatment safety. Systems reviewed: cardiovascular, respiratory, CNS, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, endocrine — plus allergies, medications, hospitalisations and pregnancy.
